purpose: Ownership, privacy, provenance and disclosure controls for applications that retrieve or store sensitive personal memory.
requirements: Memory retrieval begins from a verified authenticated identity; client-supplied user identifiers are not treated as authority.
Every retrieved memory remains scoped to its canonical owner identity and authorised application domain.
Source access is explicitly permitted before retrieval; arbitrary table or source names cannot bypass the domain boundary.
Cross-user memory disclosure fails closed unless a reviewed sharing relationship and explicit owner permission permit a bounded view.
Highly sensitive and private records are classified before disclosure and may be blocked, redacted or summarised according to policy.
Credentials, tokens, direct identifiers and internal prompts are removed from application-facing memory records.
Private recovery, journal, Step-work, health, legal and financial memory receives stricter handling than ordinary profile context.
Retrieved records preserve source and provenance metadata so model-generated text does not silently become authoritative memory.
Memory writes and promotions preserve ownership, source and lifecycle state and cannot be authorised solely by model output.
Retrieval limits and result normalisation are bounded, and unavailable retrieval remains explicit rather than fabricated.
Database row-level security or equivalent server-side ownership enforcement protects persisted personal memory.
Security and privacy tests cover authenticated ownership, cross-user denial and sensitive-field filtering.
When identity, ownership, source permission or privacy classification cannot be established, memory access fails closed.
nonClaims: This policy does not guarantee that stored memories are factually correct.
This policy does not authorise sharing merely because two people have a relationship.
This policy does not make model-generated summaries equivalent to original records.
This policy does not permit recovery or health memory to bypass application-specific safety boundaries.
